clue.text: Two jerks get car going

parts.note: a jump is a sudden jerk or twitch
a start is a sudden involuntary jerk, as when frightened

explanation.surface: Two sharp tugs are what it takes to coax a reluctant car into life.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase 'Two jerks' supplies both halves: two different words for a jerk, set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump-start a car is to start its engine using leads from another battery or by pushing it.

clue.text: Wag card

definitions.meaning: a wag is a ..., someone who likes to make jokes
an extra card in a pack, often used as a wild card

explanation.definitionFit: A wag is a habitual jester, and the extra wild playing card in a pack bears the same name.

clue.text: Driving competition properly includes time spent in particular vehicle by novice driver

indicators.note: includes says the word for properly holds the rest of the wordplay within it

parts.note: to behave properly is to behave morally

indicators.note: time spent in a vehicle is time inside it, so the abbreviation for time goes within the words for the vehicle

parts.note: a particular vehicle is one car, a single specific one
L is the learner plate worn by a novice driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A rally of proper driving that also counts the hours a learner spends in one car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent in' puts T inside ONE CAR to give ONTECAR; add L, and 'includes' places ONTECARL inside MORALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monte Carlo Rally is a famous annual motor-racing event run on roads around Monaco.

clue.text: Military featuring in report, with considerable violence

indicators.note: featuring in a report means appearing inside it, so the abbreviation goes within the word for report

parts.note: a story is a news report

explanation.surface: Army matters appearing in a news report, told with great force.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormily describes doing something in a wild, tempestuous manner, like a gale.

clue.text: Against, principally, any new Tory ideas

indicators.note: principally suggests taking the principal, leading letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A politician declares opposition, in the main, to any fresh Conservative policies.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition meaning opposed to, as in being anti war.

clue.text: Time's beginning today — there's a new order

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order means rearranging them

parts.note: the possessive-looking 's is a link here, leaving the word there as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone announces that from today a fresh regime is starting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'there's a new order' as a political announcement; 'new order' is the anagram signal for TODAY plus THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The year dot is an idiom for the very beginning of time, as in since the year dot.

clue.text: Man goes outside wearing coat

indicators.note: goes outside says the word for man is placed around the other piece

parts.note: Pat is a man's name, short for Patrick
someone in a garment is wearing it, so wearing gives in

explanation.surface: A man heads out of doors with his coat on.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint a surface is to cover it with a layer, so it works as a verb meaning to apply a layer.

clue.text: Continue to bat, and throw your wicket away

definitions.meaning: to keep going, here to carry on batting, is to keep playing
in cricket, a batsman who plays on deflects the ball off the bat onto his own stumps and is out

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to carry on, and in cricket it also names being bowled by edging the ball onto your own stumps.

clue.text: Playing another country at home, four-nil thrashing is received

annotationWithheld.why: Playing another country at home, four-nil thrashing is received (15): the definition is 'Playing another country' but no parse of 'at home, four-nil thrashing is received' gives INTERNATIONALLY (no F or U for an anagram of four-nil); web search finds the same text and no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: Playing another country at home, four-nil thrashing is received

clue.text: Remedy provided by engineer to hole in the wall, under cover

indicators.note: something under cover is sheltered inside it, so the pieces go within the word for cover

parts.note: a tent is a canvas cover or shelter
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
hole in the wall is British slang for a cash machine, an ATM

explanation.surface: An engineer's fix for a hole in a wall, carried out under a tarpaulin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole in the wall' looks like a building defect, but it is British slang for a cash machine; 'under' (as in under cover) is the signal for putting the pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the medical care or cure given for an illness or injury.

clue.text: Game honcho

definitions.meaning: a children's game in which one player holds a mound against all comers
a honcho is the boss, the person in charge

explanation.definitionFit: It is a playground game of defending a hill, and by extension a phrase for whoever is top dog.

clue.text: Papers read out in city

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the word for papers is heard rather than seen

parts.note: reams are large quantities of paper, 500 sheets each

explanation.surface: Newspapers are read aloud somewhere in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims, also spelt Reims, is a cathedral city in the Champagne region of France.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance about comeback for American politician

indicators.note: about means around, so the word of annoyance encloses the other piece

parts.note: drat is a mild exclamation of irritation
read as come back, the word come is written in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone mutters in irritation over a politician's return to the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' looks like a political return, but it is read as two words: 'come', written backwards because of 'back'. 'about' is the signal for wrapping the word of annoyance around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the Democratic Party, one of the two main US parties.

clue.text: Terribly poor sitcom I set in print room

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly mangled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful television comedy is being produced in a printing works.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: the worker says what they do, setting type in the print room.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor is a typesetter, the person who arranges type for printing.

clue.text: Plain about oarsmen using arms and legs

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for plain is written backwards

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain in South America
fours are rowing boats crewed by four oarsmen, and the crews themselves

explanation.surface: Rowers crossing a plain by crawling along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective meaning simple, but it is the noun for a South American grassland, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawling on hands and knees, with every limb touching the ground, is moving like a quadruped.

clue.text: Trumps higher, with amazing fervour, and rising with sudden emphasis

indicators.note: amazing suggests something astonishing, so the letters of fervour are thrown into disorder
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the abbreviation is written in reverse

parts.note: SF is sforzando, the musical direction for a sudden strong accent

explanation.surface: A card player trumps with great passion and a sudden flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' rearranges FERVOUR into OVERRUF; 'rising' turns SF (sforzando) into FS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or whist, to overruff is to play a higher trump on a trick another opponent has already trumped.

clue.text: Found bed low

definitions.meaning: to found something is to establish it on a footing, to ground it
a bed is a foundation layer something rests on
low here means mean or ignoble in character

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means establish on something; as a noun a foundation; as an adjective ignoble or mean.

clue.text: Tree-climbing groom

parts.note: a spruce is a coniferous tree
climbing means going up

explanation.surface: A stable lad shins up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up is to smarten oneself, the way one might tidy hair and clothes.

clue.text: Fish found in only two-thirds of fish baskets

indicators.note: keeping only two-thirds of the six-letter word means dropping its first third

parts.note: creels are wicker baskets used by anglers to carry fish

explanation.surface: Only some of the fish make it into the anglers' baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: The basket word has six letters, so two-thirds is four: its first two letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish, such as the conger or moray.

clue.text: Partly how cones taper

definitions.meaning: partly means to some extent but not entirely
a cone narrows from its base until it reaches a tip

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to a limited degree, and taken literally it describes a cone narrowing towards its tip.

clue.text: A liberal chap finds a niche

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal, as in the British party
cove is old British slang for a chap or fellow

explanation.surface: A broad-minded man discovers a recess in the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess set back into a wall of a room.

clue.text: Countryman needing game runs to a catalogue

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: A rustic fellow wants a game that runs to a whole catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruralist is someone who lives in or champions life in rural areas.

clue.text: Suitable girl taken back on as a governess

parts.note: due means fitting or appropriate, as in due respect

indicators.note: taken back means turned around, so the girl's name is written backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fitting young woman is re-employed as a governess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' looks like re-hiring the girl but turns ANN into NNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone to girls in a Spanish or Portuguese family.

clue.text: In river, river horse

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A horse is standing in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is not an animal but a clothes horse, a frame for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a frame for drying clothes, also called a clothes horse.

clue.text: It helps cobbler stay at the back

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker's foot-shaped block for shaping footwear
to stay here is to endure or keep going
at the back means coming at the end, after all the others

explanation.definitionFit: A shoemaker shapes shoes on this wooden model; it also means to endure, and final in order.

clue.text: Communist sympathiser, like gypsy

definitions.meaning: someone who supports the Communist cause without joining the party
gypsies are known as travellers, so someone like a gypsy is another of the same kind

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a non-member who backs a party line, and literally a companion on the road like a roaming Romany.

clue.text: Cut dash with name

definitions.meaning: a cut is the way hair is shaped, a hairdo
to name someone is to call or title them

explanation.definitionFit: It means a haircut, elegance or flair, and as a verb to designate someone by a title.

clue.text: A rare type, surprisingly — one funding local government

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a person who actually pays local taxes is unusually uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratepayer paid rates, the British property tax that funded local councils.
